title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
event_hint: SAC system release: CXL-based disaggregated KV cache for sparse attention LLMs
problem: RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache systems perform full prefix cache fetching before decoding, causing transmission bottlenecks and local memory waste for sparse attention models where only a small fraction of KV entries are active
mechanism: CXL-based disaggregated memory with cache-line granularity load/store semantics enables on-demand fetching of only required top-k KV entries during inference

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens, Round-2 decoding with 64 concurrency

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 9.7x lower TTFT (Time to First Token) compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens, Round-2 decoding with 64 concurrency

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 1.8x lower TBT (Time Between Token) compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens, Round-2 decoding with 64 concurrency

evidence.claim: SAC achieves throughput within 91% of local DRAM upper bound baseline
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, 8-H20 GPU server, 2TB CXL memory pool, SGLang and HiSparse framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: CXL-based disaggregated memory achieves 1.04-1.64x of local DRAM latency for sparse KV retrieval
evidence.condition: Sparse KV indices sampled from 128K-token context, DeepSeek-V3.2 MLA KV entry (512-dim latent + 64-dim RoPE, bfloat16)

evaluation_context: DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse attention model (AWQ 4-bit quantization) evaluated on 8-H20 GPU server with 2TB CXL memory pool using SGLang and HiSparse framework; two-round experimental design: Round-1 (Cache Populate) with concurrency 8 for prefill stage, Round-2 (Cache Hit) with concurrency 64 for decode stage; context lengths swept from 16K to 128K tokens with output lengths of 1K, 4K, and 8K tokens; workload from ShareGPT dataset (512 requests); comparisons against RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool and local host DRAM upper bound; Section 3.1 shows only 21% of KV cache utilized in 128K-context scenarios; device interleaving analysis shows throughput gains from multiple CXL devices; HiSparse buffer size tuning (4K vs 6K) shows 10.4% throughput improvement with larger buffer
limitations: Evidence limited to abstract/introduction/motivation/evaluation sections; detailed experimental methodology in Appendix A not reviewed; specific CXL hardware generation (2.0/3.0) not specified; RDMA network hardware details (RNIC speed, fabric configuration) not provided in supplement; MoonCache and LMCache baseline configurations not mentioned in supplement; scalability beyond 128K context not addressed; detailed memory usage breakdown not provided
project_relevance: Directly addresses memory semantics question by demonstrating how CXL's cache-line granularity load/store semantics enable fundamentally different disaggregated memory access patterns compared to RDMA's message-based send/recv model; shows 1.04-1.64x DRAM-equivalent latency for sparse access and 91% of DRAM throughput; validates CXL memory semantics for fine-grained, sparse KV access; DSA/IAA relevance indirect - work focuses on CXL fabric not CPU offload; end-to-end evidence from SGLang integration with 2.1x throughput, 9.7x TTFT, 1.8x TBT improvements on 8-H20 GPU server with 2TB CXL memory pool

evidence_gaps.question: What are the exact hardware configurations for CXL memory, GPU instances, and RDMA network used in end-to-end evaluation?
What are the detailed baseline configurations for RDMA-based disaggregated systems being compared?
